title: Shiv — Listen
description: Private taste feed: episodes only from Shiv's follow list. Curated for Apple Podcasts.
author: Shivanshu Chaudhary

items.title: How to Make a Difference: Part 1
items.description: Seligman on learned helplessness vs explanatory style — densifier on how the story you tell about a setback either freezes agency or reopens it.

items.title: Episode #189 ... Everything that connects us is slowly disappearing. - Byung Chul Han pt. 2
items.description: Byung-Chul Han on the disappearance of rituals, truth, community, and public space — densifier on why connection thins and why being an 'idiot' (unoptimized) still matters.

items.title: 368 | Elizabeth Alexander on Why Democracy Needs Imagination
items.description: Poet Elizabeth Alexander on why literature and close reading build the empathy democracy needs — craft of language as civic infrastructure.

items.title: The Art of True Happiness | Dr. Arthur Brooks
items.description:
Craft move: Brooks treats happiness as three measurable macronutrients (enjoyment, satisfaction, meaning) you can audit — not a vibe to chase.
Sharpens taste: forces a founder-grade scoreboard on interior life instead of doomscrolling mood or productivity cosplay.

items.title: The Death of Reading (with James Marriott)
items.description:
Literacy as civilizational infrastructure: Marriott maps how deep reading trained patience, abstraction, and the private mind — and what thins when the feed replaces the page.
Craft move: treat attention as a scarce production input, not a vibe.

items.title: 707. The Terror: An Assassination in Paris (Part 1)
items.description: Pure history reset: Marat’s murder as the spark that turns factional rhetoric into the Terror. How political storytelling manufactures bloodlust.

items.title: Episode #252 ... Slaughterhouse-Five - Kurt Vonnegut
items.description:
Today we talk about Kurt Vonnegut's book Slaughterhouse-Five. How war stories can distort the reality of war, how trauma can fracture our experience of time and identity, and why Billy Pilgrim becomes attracted to the strange philosophy of the Tralfamadorians.

Vonnegut's fractured time isn't a sci-fi gimmick — it's how trauma rewrites narrative causality.
Craft move: philosophy through novel structure, not treatise — watch how Billy Pilgrim's Tralfamadorian 'unstuck' becomes a thesis on war storytelling.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/episode-252-slaughterhouse-five-kurt-vonnegut/id659155419?i=1000786665460

items.title: 366 | Jim Al-Khalili on Time, Quantum, Biology, and Cosmology
items.show: Sean Carroll's Mindscape: Science, Society, Philosophy, Culture, Arts, and Ideas
items.description:
Everyone lives through time, but we continue to struggle to fully understand it. We remain unsure whether time is fundamental or emergent, why it has an arrow pointing from past to future, and how that arrow connects to our experience of time's passage. Jim Al-Khalili's new book is On Time: The Physics that Makes the Universe Tick. We discuss what time is at the most basic level, and how it connects to open questions in biology, cosmology, and quantum mechanics.

Why this sharpens your taste: watch how Al-Khalili refuses to treat “time’s arrow” as one puzzle — he forces the link between thermodynamics, quantum measurement, and biological clocks. Craft move: densify by mapping one concept across disciplines instead of stacking metaphors.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/366-jim-al-khalili-on-time-quantum-biology-and-cosmology/id1406534739?i=1000786961179

items.title: The Home Depot
items.description:
The Home Depot's founding story is like an Avengers movie… if the Avengers got fired, went broke, and stacked empty paint cans ten feet high to look legitimate. After being unceremoniously fired from their previous hardware chain at ages 48 and 35, Bernie Marcus and Arthur Blank took the words of their New York banker Ken Langone (who had also just accidentally caused their firings) to heart: they'd just been "kicked in the ass with a golden horseshoe.” They proceeded to author the greatest compounding story in American retail history, helped by some legendary cameos along the way from Sol Price, Jamie Dimon, and Ross Perot (to name a few). And the ending is as good as any superhero film: from its 1981 IPO to today, The Home Depot has been the single highest-returning equity in the entire US stock market — higher than Apple, Microsoft, Berkshire Hathaway, and everything else! Sponsors: M

Why this sharpens your taste: Acquired treats the Home Depot founding like ops theater — fired execs, empty paint-can stagecraft, then density + SKU discipline as the real moat.
Craft move: watch how Ben & David reverse-engineer a category-killer from constraints, not vibes — founder ops without the TED gloss.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/the-home-depot/id1050462261?i=1000789467893&uo=4

items.title: Francine Prose: This Is What a Harvard Writing Masterclass Feels Like | How I Write
items.description:
Francine Prose has written more than 30 books and taught at both Harvard and Bard College. If you ask her how to become a better writer, she'll tell you to start by reading like a writer. Look at words and sentences, characters and details. Study them, dissect them. Then find books that you love, ones that have stood the test of time, and ask yourself: Why has this book endured? Why has it stayed popular for so long?

But how do you actually do that? This interview provides an answer.

Why this sharpens your taste: "read like a writer" is a craft move — treat sentences as dissectable mechanism, not mood.
Ask the endurance question (why this book lasted) and reverse-engineer durability instead of collecting voice tips.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/francine-prose-this-is-what-a-harvard-writing/id1700171470?i=1000790031658

items.title: #433 How Michael Bloomberg Works
items.description:
What I learned from reading Bloomberg by Michael Bloomberg.

why this sharpens your taste:
1) Senra’s craft: compress an operator’s whole work system into transferable heuristics — Bloomberg as attention architecture, not just a product story.
2) Trains you to study HOW someone works (calendar, information diet, decision hygiene) instead of only what they built.

Apple Podcasts: https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/433-how-michael-bloomberg-works/id1141877104?i=1000789605191
